messages:
Tessa Morgan: Dropping feedback from yesterday’s walkthrough of the experiment results dashboard. Overall direction is good, but charts are still hard to “read at a glance” esp when there are 3 variants + multiple metrics.

Tessa Morgan: Biggest issue: the variant colors are too similar + the legend is far from the data. When the chart is busy, I can’t tell which line corresponds to which variant without hunting.

Alicia Perez: +1. Also, the delta chips (e.g. “+12% p95”) in the header fight visually w/ the chart legend. I was looking at the chip thinking it’s the legend.

Kenji Nakamura: For drill-down: right now clicking on a variant line takes you to a new page w/ filters. It felt like I lost context (what time window / which route). Can we do an in-place drill-down panel?

Felix Schneider: Yeah, current behavior: click line -> navigates to `/experiments/:id/results?variant=B&metric=p95_latency` etc. We can swap to a right-side drawer without leaving page.

Dylan Brooks: From eng side: drawer is doable as long as it doesn’t trigger a whole new query per hover. Click-to-open is fine.

Alicia Perez: Specific readability notes:
- Gridlines + axis labels are super faint. p99 latency chart looked like “random spaghetti” in the screenshot.
- We should default to “Control vs Variant” comparison mode. Showing all variants at once is useful, but it should be an explicit switch.

Tessa Morgan: Agree. Proposed structure:
1) Summary header (guardrail status + primary deltas)
2) Comparison section (pick a variant; show vs control)
3) “All variants” advanced view

Kenji Nakamura: Also the time series charts need a clear “guardrail threshold” line when relevant (error rate, p99). Right now the banner says “breached” but the chart doesn’t show the threshold visually.

Felix Schneider: We have the threshold value in the API response for guardrails. I can render a horizontal dashed line + label.

Marissa Cole: PM perspective: priority is “are we safe?” then “is it better?” so the guardrail line + clearer callouts helps. A/B testing is scary; should not require reading charts to detect risk.

Alicia Perez: Drill-down interactions:
- Clicking a point should open a panel w/ that timestamp bucket details (route, region breakdown, request count, error count).
- Need a quick way to pivot dimension: route (template), model_id, region.

Kenji Nakamura: For pivot, could be a segmented control: `All` | `By region` | `By model` | `By route`.

Dylan Brooks: FYI “By route” could explode. We should cap to top N and provide search.

Felix Schneider: Yep, top 10 by traffic for selected time window, then “View more” -> table view.

Tessa Morgan: Another thing: y-axis scaling. Today p50/p95/p99 charts use different scales so it’s hard to compare. For p50/p95/p99 we should keep units consistent + make it obvious when the scale changes. Maybe a small “ms” label next to the metric and a toggle between `ms` / `% change`.

Alicia Perez: + add “absolute vs delta” toggle. Deltas are great but sometimes you need absolute values to sanity-check.

Felix Schneider: We can add `Absolute | Δ vs control` toggle per chart. In Δ mode, we can center y-axis around 0 with a subtle baseline.

Kenji Nakamura: Please add “traffic share” somewhere near charts. If Variant C is 1% traffic, the line shouldn’t look equivalent weight to control.

Marissa Cole: Yes. Also add sample size / request count in the header near the time window selector.

Tessa Morgan: Accessibility: palette needs to be colorblind safe and consistent across the app. Variants should keep same colors across charts + across pages (list view -> detail -> drilldown).

Felix Schneider: Noted. We can map `control=gray`, variants from existing Rollouts palette. Also persist mapping in URL params so a refresh doesn’t reshuffle.

Alicia Perez: Small UX: legend should be clickable to isolate a series (hide others). Standard Grafana behavior. Helps declutter.

Felix Schneider: We can implement click legend -> toggle visibility. Double-click -> isolate.

Dylan Brooks: Please confirm we don’t need hover tooltips for every point (perf). Tooltip on nearest point while moving mouse is heavy for high-res timeseries.

Alicia Perez: Click-to-inspect is fine. Hover tooltip only for the header summary chips maybe.

Kenji Nakamura: Another confusing spot: “Quality” chart is shown next to latency/cost, but quality is sparse (sampled). Needs different visual treatment (e.g. dots + confidence / sample size). Otherwise it looks like missing data.

Marissa Cole: +1 and copy needs to say it’s sampled + from evals. We got feedback that people interpret it as “model quality” always present.

Tessa Morgan: Action items / follow-ups (please correct owners):
- [Felix] Switch drill-down interaction to right-side drawer (keep context), click-to-open only
- [Felix] Add guardrail threshold lines + labels on relevant charts
- [Alicia] Provide updated palette + variant color mapping guidance (control vs variants)
- [Kenji] Mock “Control vs selected variant” default mode + toggle to “All variants”
- [Felix + Dylan] Add legend click-to-isolate behavior + ensure perf is ok
- [Alicia] Define treatment for Quality metric (sample size display, dots vs line)
- [Marissa] Confirm which 2-3 metrics we feature in the summary header by default (latency p95? cost/token? error rate?)

Dylan Brooks: Looks right. For perf, we’ll also likely need to downsample points server-side for long windows (7d/30d). I’ll sync w/ Felix separately.

Felix Schneider: :thumbsup: I’ll file eng tasks and link here. For the drawer, I’ll reuse the audit log drawer component if possible.

Alicia Perez: I’ll share palette + updated legend placement ideas by EOD tomorrow.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll update the Figma flow w/ the compare-first layout and tag y’all.

Marissa Cole: Thanks. Let’s aim to land the “compare-first + guardrail lines + better colors” before expanding beta. That’s what keeps coming up in calls.

Tessa Morgan: Cool. I’ll mark these as required for “beta readiness” in the design checklist. (Also adding note: axis labels need to be at least 12px + higher contrast.)
